content:
Spotify today announced an expansion of its previously launched "User Notes" feature. Originally, "User Notes" was only applicable to songs, while the new "Playlist Notes" allows users to add annotations to Podcast episodes and audiobooks within playlists. Details are as follows.

"Record memories, share recommendations, or explain why you chose this song"

Last month, Spotify launched "User Notes," a social feature that allows users to add a short note of up to 240 characters to individual songs within their playlists.

Today, according to an exclusive report by TechCrunch, Spotify announced the launch of "Playlist Notes," further expanding the application scope of "User Notes."

Through "Playlist Notes," users can now, in addition to adding notes to songs, also add annotations to Podcast episodes and audiobooks that have been added to playlists.

Spotify stated that its editorial team will also use "Playlist Notes" to "share the significance of a song, its cultural meaning, or why this song is suitable for inclusion in this particular playlist."

Users can also browse "Editor Profiles" to "learn about the creative team behind the playlists," where they can also see the editors' favourite songs, favourite albums, and the playlists they oversee.

Below is the official tutorial from Spotify on adding "Playlist Notes":

The "Playlist Notes" feature for user-curated playlists is currently rolling out in over 100 markets worldwide, available on iOS and Android platforms. Actual availability may vary from the editorial team's "Playlist Notes." Please open a playlist you own or co-edit. Tap the three-dot icon (…) next to a song, podcast episode, or audiobook you have added to the playlist. Select "Add note." Type what you want to write, then tap "Save."

Spotify stated that "Editor Profiles" and their "Playlist Notes" will begin rolling out today to all users aged 16 and above in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.
